name: section-depth-limit
body: No template composition chain may be deeper than six heading levels (`#` through `######`): heading depth is nesting depth, so a section at depth n has children at depth n+1 only, and the depth is bounded by the content syntax, not a setting. Levels are counted from the top-level section's `#` heading: the top-level section's `#` heading is level one, and the slide itself contributes no heading level. A template set whose composition depth exceeds six is refused at load with a templates error path-qualified to the offending `template.yaml` (templates-dir-validation step 4). A bounded self-nesting chain (requirements.requirement.bounded-self-nesting) counts toward this bound: the loader walks each declared-section cycle it accepts to its full `max_depth`, and the heading-level length of the chain that walk produces — the cycle's composition prefix plus one heading per bounded level — is what the six-level bound measures. A cycle whose full walk would exceed six heading levels is refused at load with the depth-limit error naming the chain and the `max_depth` that produces it, so every declared `max_depth` is reachable in content. A `section` helper call and its child arguments participate in cycle rejection but are not headings, so they do not by themselves extend this heading-level chain (template-composition, section-helper-load-checks, child-constructor).
